findings.claim: DISCLOSURE: docs/wiki/config-reference.md:313 says leading redirections are skipped to the program; BARE_REDIRECTION/GLUED_REDIRECTION omit >|, bare <> and {fd}>, so those leading forms leave the program unread.
findings.counterexample: Bash, deny row 'pnpm db:migrate:prod': '>|log pnpm db:migrate:prod', '>| log ...', '2>|x ...', '<> f ...', '{fd}>log ...' -> allow no-policy-match each; '>|x sh -c "pnpm db:migrate:prod"' -> allow (no opaque warn); control '>log pnpm db:migrate:prod' -> deny

findings.claim: DISCLOSURE: docs/wiki/config-reference.md:337 says a quoted first non-option argument with no -File is a string; firstPositionalIsQuoted stops at an option's value, and Windows PowerShell's unquoted positional (default -Command) is not read; the -ExecutionPolicy limit is stated only in the code comment.
findings.counterexample: 'powershell -nop -w hidden "Remove-Item x"' -> allow; 'powershell Remove-Item x' -> allow; 'pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass "x"' -> allow. Measured on Windows PowerShell 5.1: an unquoted positional and the -w hidden quoted form both run as commands; pwsh 7 reads a positional as -File, so the 'pwsh "x"' warn is a harmless false positive.

findings.claim: DISCLOSURE (existed before this fold): a partially quoted heredoc delimiter makes the body literal in bash, but the reader treats it as unquoted and reads substitutions there.
findings.counterexample: Bash, deny row 'pnpm db:migrate:prod': cat <<E\OF / cat <<E'O'F with $(pnpm db:migrate:prod) in the body -> deny on both the old and new code (bash expands nothing); cat <<"E"OF -> allow

findings.claim: DISCLOSURE: the load refusal and the runtime skip both match wrappers by basename, so a repository script named env, time, command, nice and so on can never be governed, and the refusal text 'drop the leading wrapper' misleads.
findings.counterexample: patterns 'scripts/env', './env deploy', './time' -> refused at load; at runtime './scripts/env pnpm db:migrate:prod' -> deny m (the script is skipped as the env wrapper)

findings.claim: TEST PIN: no head test uses a subject between 513 and 1024 characters, so reverting ACTION_POLICY_WILDCARD_TOKEN_MAX to 1024 fails no test; the overridden-warn wrapper test covers --strict only.
findings.counterexample: Head tests use 1100-character subjects; the same shapes pass on the old code (1024 head): 'run *z' against 'run '+1100 a's+'z' -> no-policy-match on both. Pilot tier measured end to end: exit 0, one additionalContext object; not pinned.

verdict: Read 4 of the action-policy gate, scoped to the two commits after the third read (7c177575, the fold of read 3 plus the override change; 72bf6988, the CI fix), which had gone to the pull request with no independent read: blocking=0 material=0 minor=5 question=0 folded=5 (counts as typed). CONVERGED by the read's own line. Held, measured: the raw heredoc-body reader with bash's backslash escape honoured and every quoted-delimiter form literal; the PowerShell opener rule (an odd backtick run escapes, a backslash does not, single quotes literal); the leading-redirection and coproc skip on fourteen forms with no program movement on a redirection after the program; the closed shell list, the colon spellings and the quoted positional; the dead-pattern refusals; the override returning warn through the real wrapper at both tiers with one context object, and a strict deny still exit 2; the 512 head at about 12 ms for a three-star glob against a 1000-character subject; the shield opt-in pin asserting the exact call-site argument lists; both shield suites green and an 8,400-input differential with zero verdict changes.
